svg.aria-label: How to write к: one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
svg.title: Writing к
svg.desc: 3 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of к (cyrillic), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase к demonstration, 04:45–04:51, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source note on variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 04:45–04:51 lowercase к demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends the left stem to the baseline, turns upward through a looped upper-right arm, returns to the middle junction, continues down and right through the lower arm, and finishes through a small rising exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand has a rounded, looped upper arm plus entry and exit joins; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed form with a straight vertical stem and two angular diagonal arms, without the cursive joins. This learner path preserves the source's left-stem-to-upper-arm-to-lower-arm order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, retrace upward through the middle, trace the upper diagonal out and back, then continue through the lower diagonal without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's rounded upper loop and entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant either arm differently.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
